title: Evaluation of the influence of building façade design on the acoustic characteristics and auditory perception of urban spaces
research_question: This study focuses on the influence of façade design on acoustic characteristics of an urban space and on the subjective spatial perception of the users, specifically assessing the influence of different characteristics of façade upholsteries on the auditory perception of space wideness for listeners placed in different points of a small square.

participants.description: Aged between 19 and 31 (M=24.68, SD=3.16), with normal hearing capability. From Politecnico di Torino, Italy.
participants.recruitment: Voluntary participation, recruited among colleagues with frequent experiences of the area.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: 18 auralizations of a virtual 3D model of Largo Saluzzo (a small octagonal square in Turin, Italy). These included 3 different façade materials (plain painted brickwork, coarse concrete, green wall) with varying sound absorption coefficients (0.05, 0.35, 0.70), 3 different sound scattering coefficients (0.1, 0.5, 0.9), and 2 listener positions (A: center, B: opposite corner). The sound source was an anechoic recording of chatting people.
A simplified 3D model of Largo Saluzzo, an octagonal square (2000m²) in Turin, Italy, surrounded by buildings. The model was calibrated against in situ reverberation time measurements.

mechanisms: The difference in the ratio of direct and reflected energy for different listener positions influences which acoustic parameters (T30 vs C50) are most influential for perceived space wideness.
Higher sound absorption reduces reflected sound energy, leading to lower SPL, shorter reverberation times, and increased clarity and DRR.
Sound scattering diffuses sound, affecting reverberation time, clarity, and DRR.
moderators: Listener position (distance from sound source and building façades)
implementation_implications: A more general mathematical relation between perceived wideness and acoustic parameters could be developed and used as a design rule for overall acoustic perception in urban squares.
Façade design choices can affect how spaces are perceived by users, particularly for visually impaired people who rely on auditory perception for self-orientation and movement.

limitations: The study used a limited number of listener positions (two), which restricts the generalizability of the mathematical relation between perceived wideness and acoustic parameters.
The study focused on a single sound source typology (chatting people), which may not represent the full complexity of urban soundscapes.

paper_metadata.title: Evaluation of the influence of building façade design on the acoustic characteristics and auditory perception of urban spaces
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Evaluation of the influence of building façade design on the acoustic characteristics and auditory perception of urban spaces
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Auditory perception has been proved to have an influence on how we live and move through places and on the use of public spaces. However, despite the numerous studies that have focused on the theme of soundscape and auditory perception of urban spaces, these aspects have not been studied in connection with the design of the building surrounding such spaces. This study focuses on the influence of façade design on acoustic characteristics of an urban space and on the subjective spatial perception of the users. Simulations and auralizations have been conducted through ODEON software (v.13) on the virtual model of a small square of Turin (Italy). Different absorption and scattering coefficients of façade upholsteries have been applied to the façades of the building surrounding the square, choosing from a pool of typical building façade materials. Results of a listening test have proved that the absorption coefficient of the façades has an influence on the subjective perception of space wideness. Moreover, multiple regression analysis has been conducted in order to find a mathematical relation between space wideness perception and objective acoustic parameters. It was shown that the relation between the perceptual aspects and the objective parameters is strongly dependent on the listening position.
